subject: general
question: Which ancient civilisations flourished in the Thar Desert area about 5000 years ago?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus Valley Civilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilisation, also known as Harappan Civilisation, existed approximately between 3300 BCE and 1300 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It flourished in areas of modern-day Pakistan and northwest India, including the Thar Desert region.
 
• Major sites of the civilisation include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Kalibangan, which are all located near river systems and arid regions like the Thar Desert.
 
• The civilisation is noted for its advanced urban planning, including the use of baked bricks, drainage systems, and water storage facilities.
 
• It was one of the world's earliest urban civilisations alongside Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:** The term "Indus Valley Civilisation" is derived from the Indus River, around which many of the settlements were concentrated.
 
• **Key Features:** The civilisation was known for its trade networks, craft production, and script, though the script remains undeciphered.
 
• **Climate Context:** The Thar Desert region played a role in the civilisation's adaptation strategies, including water management and agriculture in semi-arid zones.
 
• **Decline:** The decline of the civilisation is attributed to environmental changes, such as the drying up of the Sarasvati River and possible shifts in monsoon patterns.
 
• **Archaeological Evidence:** Excavations have revealed seals, pottery, jewellery, and tools that provide insights into the daily life and culture of the Indus Valley people.
